territorial_scope.description: Applies to telecommunications, broadcasting, spectrum, orbital resources and satellite services under federal jurisdiction across Mexico.

evidence.quote: son de jurisdicción federal

summary.short: Mexico's federal telecommunications and broadcasting law, published in the Diario Oficial on 16 July 2025, governs spectrum, concessions, interconnection, competition and users' rights, creates the Agency and Regulatory Commission, and repeals the earlier federal telecommunications and broadcasting law.
summary.long: The law sets the regime for telecommunications, broadcasting and satellite services, and for the radio spectrum and orbital resources, which are federal property (Art. 32). It creates the Agencia de Transformación Digital y Telecomunicaciones and, under it, the Comisión Reguladora de Telecomunicaciones, which holds broad regulatory, supervisory and sanctioning powers (Arts. 8 to 10). Providing public telecommunications and broadcasting services requires a single concession (Arts. 45 and 46). Spectrum and orbital concessions for commercial use are generally awarded by public tender (Arts. 57 and 71), with terms of up to 30 years for the single concession (Art. 51) and up to 20 years for spectrum and orbital concessions (Art. 54). Concessionaires must interconnect on non-discriminatory terms under Commission-set tariffs and conditions, and preponderant or substantial-power economic agents face specific obligations (Arts. 110 to 123). Foreign investment in concessionaires is limited (Arts. 50 and 56). Mobile lines may be activated only for users who present official identification (Art. 103). The Commission supervises children's programming and audience rights (Art. 10). Internet access providers must respect contracted capacity and content neutrality (Art. 132). Non-compliance is sanctioned by the Commission (Art. 10). This part covers Articles 1 to 144.

notes: This part covers Arts. 1-140 (purpose, authorities, spectrum, concessions, interconnection and satellite provisions). Relations are mainly supplementary-law references and cross-references; no registry IDs are assigned, so target_instrument_id is empty. Possible overlap, not stated as a conflict: Art. 10 fr. XV and Art. 116 give the Comisión power over interconnection tariffs, while Art. 124 has the Agencia set terms and tariffs for interconnection of public and social concessionaires. Enforcement, obligations and thresholds are not coded in this part. Part 2 of 3 covers Arts. 141-298 (Títulos Quinto to Décimo Quinto). Terms such as Comisión and Agencia are defined in Part 1, so their full names are not given here. Relations target instruments not in the registry, so target_instrument_id is an empty string (schema requires a string; codebook says null). Art. 245 contains a garbled tax reference. Art. 149 fracciones I and II repeat the same text. Art. 280 fracción I contains a drafting error ('del valor diario de la de Unidad'). Penalties in Arts. 281-295 are not coded here (enforcement annotated in the full text's annotation). Part 3 covers Article 299 and the Transitorios only. Most transitional dates depend on the CRT Pleno being integrated, a date this part does not give. Transitorio Vigésimo Segundo says 'hasta el año siguiente' without a fixed start for the year. Units differ: Transitorio Segundo and Vigésimo Séptimo use días naturales, while Vigésimo, Trigésimo and Trigésimo Segundo use días hábiles. The text calls the law itself 'Decreto' throughout, and the 2024 constitutional decree is also called 'Decreto'. Concession holders and other regulated firms are named only generically, so they are not coded as entities.
